currentContext.business: The Company is domiciled in India with its registered office in Mumbai and is engaged in the manufacturing of specialty chemicals, with manufacturing carried out from plants at Dahej (Gujarat) and Kurkumbh, District Pune (Maharashtra). It has decades of experience in specialty chemicals including surfactants and performance additives, and has built customer relationships across textiles, agrochemicals, personal care and oilfield chemicals. Its technical expertise and manufacturing capabilities, particularly in oilfield chemicals and polymer additives, position it as a quality-focused supplier in performance chemicals, and it serves both domestic and export markets.

currentContext.strengths: Multipurpose manufacturing facilities that allow the Company to pivot using alternate raw materials as needed|Access to advanced Japanese technologies and global expertise, enhancing technical capabilities and credibility|Decades of experience in specialty chemicals, including surfactants and performance additives, with strong long-standing customer relationships|Strong technical expertise and manufacturing capability in oilfield chemicals and polymer additives, positioning it as a reliable and quality-focused supplier|Long term off-take agreements used to stabilize the chain between suppliers and customers|Portfolio of value-added and environmentally compliant products that has supported margin expansion and enabled presence in Southeast Asia, Africa and Europe|Strict liquidity discipline maintained to navigate industry cycles
currentContext.strategies: Mitigate raw-material and supply-chain risk through dual sourcing and proactive market monitoring backed by strategic planning|Use multipurpose manufacturing facilities to pivot to alternate raw materials as market conditions require|Use long term off-take agreements commercially to stabilize the chain between suppliers and customers|Maintain strict liquidity financially in order to navigate industry cycles|Leverage AI and digital tools to enhance data analysis and decision-making|The routed governance sections do not set out a dividend or payout policy. The stated capital-allocation intent is reinvestment into the manufacturing and innovation base: management describes FY2025-26 as a year of investment across operations, technology and the product portfolio to strengthen competitive position, with a key milestone being the expansion of ethoxylation capacity through the addition of a new EO reactor at the Dahej facility - framed as a strategic investment that strengthens the manufacturing platform, enhances operational flexibility and broadens the range of specialty chemical applications served. Alongside this, the Company continued to modernise production infrastructure, strengthen manufacturing systems, and invest in application development and customer-focused innovation, including the commissioning of a dedicated Agrochemical Application Laboratory. Governance framing is that good corporate governance leads to long term shareholder value; CSR spending became applicable during FY2025-26 because net profit exceeded the prescribed statutory threshold in the preceding financial year, and the Board modified the CSR Policy on August 7, 2025.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's central expansion move is the doubling of capacity in its major area of operation, Ethoxylation, with the expanded capacity directed towards some of its major oilfield initiatives - management frames this as delivering both growth and a competitive advantage. During FY2025-26 the Company progressed these capacity expansion initiatives, including enhancement of ethoxylation capabilities and strengthening of manufacturing infrastructure to support future growth, alongside operational efficiency gains from better process controls, energy optimization and reduction in non-standard batch materials. On the innovation side, the Company established an Application Development laboratory in the agriculture chemicals space to strengthen customer-centric product development and commercialization, and has started working on logistics and procurement initiatives based on AI. No commissioning date, project cost or dated completion timeline for the ethoxylation expansion is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and the resulting commodity and logistics shock
risks.note: Management calls global uncertainty the new normal, driven by the Russia-Ukraine and Gaza wars and the ongoing Iran-Israel conflict; these have significantly impacted commodity and logistics markets, causing sharp increases in crude oil and freight costs and exposing global supply chains to continuous disruption. Mitigation is dual sourcing, proactive market monitoring and strategic planning.

risks.risk: Feedstock dependence and pricing - naphtha, imported LPG and propane
risks.note: India remains heavily dependent on naphtha as a feedstock along with imported LPG and propane for downstream chemical production, exposing the industry to global crude, naphtha and LPG price fluctuations. Feedstock availability and pricing will remain a key constraint until India develops access to more affordable domestic gaseous hydrocarbons at scale.

risks.risk: Structural cost disadvantage versus ethane-advantaged regions
risks.note: The naphtha/LPG dependency creates cost sensitivities and competitive disadvantages compared to regions like the United States, where access to ethane-rich shale gas provides a structural cost advantage - a durable margin headwind for Indian downstream chemical producers.

risks.risk: Prolonged global chemical industry slowdown and margin compression
risks.note: The global chemical industry has faced a slowdown since 2022 driven by capacity imbalances and weaker demand across key sectors; after two decades of rapid expansion the industry is recalibrating expectations, with lower margins and reduced value creation becoming the new reality.
Significant overstocking and oversupply from China is named as a driver of the industry slowdown, pressuring pricing and demand across key chemical sectors.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and supply-chain constraints
risks.note: FY2025-26 was marked by trade disruptions, supply chain constraints, inflationary pressures and volatility in key raw material markets; the Company relies on multipurpose manufacturing facilities that allow it to pivot using alternate raw materials, and on long term off-take agreements, to absorb this.

risks.risk: Rising regulatory and compliance cost from the policy environment
risks.note: Management notes the policy environment presents a dual impact - while offering fiscal and strategic support for growth through FDI policies, PLI schemes, PCPIR clusters and decarbonization initiatives, it also introduces higher compliance costs for companies.
Management explicitly maintains strict liquidity to navigate industry cycles, indicating cycle-driven earnings and working-capital risk in a downcycle.
